lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Harborview Surf School | Surf Instructor | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Taught weekend group lessons to beginners aged 8 to 60, keeping each class to one instructor for every six students.
- Ran the rental desk's morning equipment checks and logged board and wetsuit repairs for the shop owner.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
- Improved dispute-form completion by 40% by splitting the form into three short steps with saved progress.
- Ran 18 moderated usability sessions a quarter from a recruiting panel of 400 customers, so every major release was tested with real account holders before launch.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Raised the onboarding flow's System Usability Scale score from 68 to 104 across two rounds of moderated testing with 20 customers.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Measured the redesign with timed tasks: median route-finding time fell from 95 to 62 seconds and errors from 11 to 3 across the 12 sessions.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Conducted user interviews and created wireframes for a free clinic's online booking flow.
- Ten clinic patients were recruited and two rounds of hallway testing were run, and the six issues that stopped first-time users were fixed.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA)
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interviews, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Experience is not in reverse-chronological order.
items.because: Northwind appears above the more recent Pinegrove role, making the work history harder to scan.

items.says: Experience should appear above Education.
items.because: The professional UX research work is more relevant to the current direction and should be seen sooner.

items.says: The current Harborview entry takes space from the résumé’s UX direction.
items.because: Its surf-instruction and rental-desk duties are less relevant than the UX research experience.

items.says: The lesson bullet gives no student outcome or teaching approach, and the instructor ratio is not connected to a result.
The instructor ratio is wordier than necessary.
The equipment checks and repair log have no stated operational effect or measure of usefulness.
The line incorrectly describes an average recommendation rating as Net Promoter Score.
items.because: NPS is the percentage of promoters minus the percentage of detractors, not the mean recommendation rating.

items.says: The score change does not say what you did to contribute to it.
items.because: Without the research or product work behind the change, the outcome is harder to connect to your UX research skills.

items.says: The trailing calculation explanation buries the accomplishment.
“Writes” incorrectly presents the Northwind responsibility as current.
items.because: The present tense conflicts with the role’s February 2022 end date.

items.says: The bullet does not specify what kind of testing you conducted.
The phrase about support calls is wordier than necessary.
The 40% completion increase has no stated baseline or comparison period.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it is a relative increase or a percentage-point change, or judge its scale.

items.says: The release-coverage clause does not say what the research changed or improved.
The release-coverage clause is long and adds little beyond the sessions and panel details.
The support-call result is buried, and “Synthesizing” leaves the completed-role bullet without a past-tense opening verb.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the result, and the opening participle does not match a completed role.

items.says: The 23% reduction has no stated baseline or comparison period.
The reported System Usability Scale score of 104 is outside the standard range.
items.because: Standard SUS scores range from 0 to 100.

items.says: The result about doubling tests is delayed after a long clause.
The first bullet repeats evaluation details reported below without stating a result of the redesign.
items.because: The following bullets give the measured outcomes, so repeating the testing details here adds no evidence of impact.

items.says: The second bullet repeats the testing setup and sample already given in the first bullet.
The change from 65% to 85% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% relative increase.
items.because: Relative to the original 65%, the increase is about 30.8%.

items.says: The third bullet repeats the sample size stated in the preceding bullets.
The interview and wireframe bullet does not say what the work changed.
The result about the six issues is buried after the testing details.
The passive testing description obscures your role.
